input.text:
TCK-001 asked for an optional reserve price on listings. The reserve must be at least the starting price. An auction that closes below the reserve ends unsold with no winner, and bidders only ever see whether the reserve is met, never the amount.

Requirements (P1): REQ-012 "Reserve price" is new. Its criteria cover rejecting a reserve below the starting price, the close rules, showing reserve met or not met on item pages and lists, never exposing the amount, and carrying the reserve-met state in live bid and close events. REQ-001 now lists the reserve as an optional field. REQ-004 now says the highest bidder wins only when there is no reserve or the reserve is met, and that watchers see the unsold state when there is no winner. Changing or removing a reserve after listing was added to out of scope. The phase recorded three assumptions that still need confirming:
- the reserve is entered and stored in the item currency
- whether sellers can see their own reserve amount (not covered now; nobody can see it after listing)
- items without a reserve show no reserve indicator at all

Design (P2): Item (DSN-015) gets a reservePrice attribute and two new methods, isReserveMet() and close(). There is a new PublicItem interface (DSN-044) for data sent to clients. It has a reserveMet field and no reserve amount. ItemView, ItemController and ItemService now return PublicItem, and listItem takes a reservePrice parameter. The list item, place bid and close auction scenarios (SEQ-002, SEQ-003, SEQ-005) now show the reserve parameter, the isReserveMet call and the close call. The publishers, ItemStore, LiveGateway, the components and UC-002 to UC-006 now also trace to REQ-012. One criterion was left without a design mapping: REQ-008's "no admin role". A reviewer should decide whether the design as a whole covers it.

Code (P4):
- Item checks the reserve and now holds the close logic that used to sit in ItemService.closeDueAuctions.
- ItemService rejects a reserve below the starting price and converts items to PublicItem before returning them.
- ItemStore persists the reserve. On older databases it adds the missing column at startup.
- Both event publishers add reserveMet to their payloads.
- The HTTP route passes reservePrice through, defaulting to null.
- The web client has an optional reserve field and shows "reserve met" or "reserve not met" when an item has a reserve.
- The README tables were updated to match.

The test phase (P5) updated six test files for the new constructor and listItem signatures. Typecheck failures after P4 came from tests still using the old Item and listItem signatures, not from the code. P5 also added tests for REQ-001 AC4 and AC5, the reordered REQ-004 criteria (now AC2 to AC6) and REQ-012 AC1 to AC8. Final result: 57 passed, 0 failed. The earlier P5 summary also mentioned 8 todo tests.

Still open:
- The UC-004 test for the live reserve-met state checks for a reserveMet field in the bid event. The design does not define the event payload, so this name was taken from PublicItem. It matches the code, but the payload shape is still not in the design.
- Check that the renumbered REQ-004 criteria and the updated SEQ-002, SEQ-005 and SEQ-006 scenario tests match what the requirements mean.
- No test exercises the client-side reserve display in public/index.html.

text:
I saved the change report and closed TCK-001. The final test run had 57 passed and 0 failed.

**What changed in each phase:**
- **Requirements:** REQ-012 is new and covers the reserve price. REQ-001 now lists the reserve as an optional field. REQ-004 has the new close rules: the highest bidder wins only if there is no reserve or the reserve is met, otherwise the item is unsold. Changing or removing a reserve after listing was added to out of scope.
- **Design:** Item now has a reserve price and two new methods, one that says whether the reserve is met and one that closes the auction. A new PublicItem (DSN-044) is what gets sent to clients: it shows whether the reserve is met and never the amount. The item controller, item service and item view now return it.
- **Code:** listings with a reserve below the starting price are rejected. The reserve is saved to the database, and older databases get the new column when the server starts. Live bid and close events now say whether the reserve is met. The web page has an optional reserve field and shows "reserve met" or "reserve not met".
- **Tests:** six test files were updated to the new signatures, and new tests cover the reserve rules.

**Still open:**
- **Three assumptions in the requirements need confirming:**
  - the reserve is in the item's currency
  - whether sellers can see their own reserve amount (right now nobody can after listing)
  - items without a reserve show no reserve label at all
- **"No admin role" in REQ-008 has no design element.** Someone needs to decide whether the design as a whole counts as covering it.
- **The live event's contents aren't in the design.** The UC-004 test expects a `reserveMet` field in bid events; the code sends it, but the design doesn't say it should.
- **Two things to check by hand:** the renumbered REQ-004 tests (AC2 to AC6) and the updated scenario tests for listing, closing and viewing prices (SEQ-002, SEQ-005, SEQ-006) should still match the requirements. No test covers the reserve display on the web page.
